title: CI fixers and the false-heal check
bridge: A CI fixer is like the teammate who jumps on red main: reproduce the failing job, make the smallest fix, push. Except: it must never make CI green by weakening a test. A mechanical check reads every diff for exactly that before any PR exists.
intro: Red main blocks everyone. This lesson turns on the first routines: the FE CI fixer, the BE CI fixer and the DevOps pipeline fixer. Each first asks "is it us?", reproduces the failing job in a VM, and fixes it inside its paths. The false-heal check rejects any fix that weakens a test.

picture.caption: Reproduce at main's head first; fix only if it is really the code; reject any fix that weakens a test.

steps.text: routineRun looks up how to reproduce the failed job
runs the failed commands at main's head: is it us?
green in the VM: environment or flake; post the evidence and stop
red in the VM: the smallest fix inside frontend/
every diff is read for deleted tests, skips, removed assertions, looser thresholds
clean: the scope judge with the charter; any finding rejects the run

sections.h: The FE CI fixer: is it us?
p: When [FRONTEND] - CI fails on main, one run per root cause starts fe-ci-fixer (lesson g5-2). Its first step is always the same question: is it us? It runs the failed commands at main's head in the VM.

Green in the VM means the environment or a flake, not the code. The run posts the evidence to #ai-agents-alerts and stops. Red in the VM means a real failure, and the agent makes the smallest fix inside frontend/.
jobs.yaml maps each frontend CI job to the commands that reproduce it, and names the jobs that are hand-offs. The fix must pass npm run verify (G7) and the reproduced commands.
sections.because: Checking main's head first avoids "fixing" code that is not broken, which is the most common way a CI fixer goes wrong.

code.text:
# ai-agents/routines/fe-ci-fixer/jobs.yaml: sketch: how each "[FRONTEND] - CI" job is reproduced in the VM
workflow: "[FRONTEND] - CI"
setup: cd frontend && npm ci                     # Node 24.15; packages through the Nexus npm proxy (G3)
check_main_first: true                           # failed commands green at main's head → environment or flake
jobs:
  "Unit Tests":
    vm: lite
    repro:
      - .github/scripts/frontend/script-tests/test-playwright-parallelism.sh
      - cd frontend && npm run check-types
      - cd frontend && npm run lint
      - cd frontend && npm run test:unit
  "Build":
    vm: lite
    repro: ["cd frontend && npm run build", "cd frontend && npm run build-storybook"]
  "Build E2E app":
    vm: full
    repro: ["<copy the build steps from .github/workflows/_frontend-build-e2e-app.yml>"]
  "I&T - AWS":
    vm: full
    repro: ["cd frontend && npx playwright test --project=pr <failed spec>   # against FCP Lab, not QA"]
    if_green_in_lab: hand_off                    # passes on Lab, failed on QA → QA env or data, not code
  "I&T - GCP": { same_as: "I&T - AWS" }
  "Deploy": { hand_off: "needs cloud credentials; DevOps" }
  "Publish": { hand_off: "image publishing; DevOps" }

notes.text: Data only: routines/ holds charters and job maps; the code lives in the harness.
Install once. Packages come through the Nexus npm proxy, since the VM has no open internet.
Run the failed commands at main's head first. Green means environment or flake.
The job's exact name in CI. Its repro steps are the same commands the job runs.
The script-tests step from frontend CI.
Needs a full VM. Copy its build steps from the reusable e2e build workflow.
Re-run only the failed spec, against FCP Lab, not the QA environment.
Passes on Lab but failed on QA: the QA environment or its data, not code.
Needs cloud credentials. The VM has none, so this is always a hand-off to DevOps.

sections.h: The BE CI fixer, part 1: cloud
p: The BE CI fixer reuses the same flow for [CLOUD] - CI and [CLIENT] - CI. Only the commands, paths and skills change. Its charter allows cloud/**, client/** and sdk/**, with **/migrations/** denied.

Some failures are always hand-offs. Protoc drift touches the stubs in common/fcp_common/, which is the cloud-client contract and outside BE routine paths. A makemigrations --check failure means a migration, and the pilot has none. Integration tests need the QA environments, which the VM cannot reach.
sections.because: Knowing in advance which failures a routine must hand off keeps it from trying fixes it is not allowed to make.

code.text:
# ai-agents/routines/be-ci-fixer/jobs.yaml: sketch: "[CLOUD] - CI" and "[CLIENT] - CI" jobs in the VM
check_main_first: true
workflows:
  "[CLOUD] - CI":
    "Lint":
      vm: lite
      repro:
        - cd cloud/rhinoCloud && uv sync --frozen --only-group lint --no-install-project
        - pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure
      hand_off_if: "the diff is in common/fcp_common/rhinoAgentRpc (protoc drift: the cloud↔client contract)"
    "Unit Tests":
      vm: full                                   # postgres, minio and redis come from the compose services
      repro:
        - ./scripts/local_run_backend_unit_tests.sh cloud <failed test label>
        - ./scripts/local_run_backend_unit_tests.sh cloud    # the whole suite before "done"
      hand_off_if: "makemigrations --dry-run --check fails (no migrations in the pilot)"
    "I&T - AWS": { hand_off: "runs on qa-cloud behind cloud_integration_tests_aws; the VM has no QA access" }
    "I&T - GCP": { hand_off: "same, behind cloud_integration_tests_gcp" }
    "Publish": { hand_off: "edits RhinoHealth/gitops; DevOps" }

notes.text: The same first question as FE: is it us?
Jobs of the cloud CI workflow, by their exact names.
Install only the lint tools, from the lockfile, without installing the project.
The lint job: black, isort and flake8 through pre-commit.
A diff under rhinoAgentRpc is the gRPC contract: hand it to people.
Unit tests need postgres, minio and redis from the compose services, so a full VM.
First the failed test, then the whole suite before done.
A missing migration: no migrations in the pilot, so hand it off.
Integration tests run on qa-cloud behind a lock; the VM has no QA access.
Publishing edits the gitops repo: DevOps.

sections.h: The BE CI fixer, part 2: client
p: The client part is the same shape, with client/rhinoOnPrem and its own integration locks. Run the BE part of the red-builds slice (lesson g5-9) 3 times before turning on shadow.
Both CI fixers use Opus 5.5 at low effort; a failed step re-runs at medium. They run on a lite Spot VM, and on a full VM when the tests need the compose services or FCP Lab.
sections.because: Backend red builds block the same people, so the BE fixer reuses the FE flow and only swaps the commands.

notes.text: The second workflow under the same workflows key.
The client's own uv project and lint group.
Client unit tests with fcp's script and the client component.
Client integration tests run on qa-on-prem: always a hand-off.

sections.h: The false-heal check, part 1: the patterns
p: A false heal is a fix that makes CI green by weakening a test. A CI fixer can always do that: delete the test, skip it, remove an assertion, raise a timeout. It is the one failure that must never ship.

false-heal.ts builds on G0-19's weakened-tests detector (ai-agents/checks/src/weakened-tests.ts): one implementation, with the charter rules added. The patterns cover both stacks, pytest and unittest, Vitest and Playwright.
For Nova, findings are flags in the PR. For routines, any finding rejects the run with outcome false_heal, and one false heal moves the routine down the trust ladder.
sections.because: A regular expression over the diff catches the mechanical forms of weakening before any model or person has to.

notes.text: Built on G0's detector, plus the charter rules.
A test file: under tests/, test/, e2e/ or integration-tests/, or named test_*.py, *_test.py, *.test.ts(x), *.spec.ts(x).
New skips: pytest skip and xfail, unittest skip, skipTest(), and .skip, .only or .fixme in Vitest and Playwright.
An assertion line: assert, self.assert...( or expect(.
A threshold with a number: fail-under, retries, timeout. Group 1 is the key, group 2 the value.
Sleeps, retry decorators and reruns: the flaky-test fixer's forbidden fixes.
How many lines match a pattern.
Is this file a test file?
A deleted test file is always a false heal.
Any added line with a skip, in any file.
Fewer assertions than before in a test file.
With this never-rule, even changing one existing assertion is a finding.

sections.h: The false-heal check, part 2: thresholds and charter rules
p: pairedChanges finds the same threshold key on a removed and an added line, with the old and new value. A fail-under that goes down is looser; a retries or timeout value that goes up is looser.
Two more charter rules. add_retries_or_sleeps is for the flaky-test fixer. add_code is for the dead-code removers, which may only delete; an import line that only loses names is fine.

The check runs in two places. In the VM, the Stop hook runs it so the agent sees the problem before it says done. Before any PR, it runs on the diff ahead of the scope judge, which gets the list with the charter.
sections.because: Running the check inside the VM lets the agent restore the test itself; running it again before the PR is the wall.

notes.text: Each threshold key that appears on a removed line and on an added line.
For fail-under, lower is looser. For retries and timeouts, higher is looser.
The finding names the key and both values.
Only when the charter forbids it: any added sleep or retry is a finding.
A deletions-only routine may shorten lines but never add new code.
Any finding gives outcome false_heal: rejected, and counted on the trust ladder.

callout.text: Agents never weaken the checks they are judged by. The false-heal check, G0's weakened-tests check and the scope judge enforce the same rule in three places.

sections.h: The pipeline fixer, part 1: workflow weakeners
p: DevOps checks are growing (G7), and red pipelines block everyone. The pipeline fixer takes red check workflows in infrastructure, gitops and fcp's .github/. It reproduces the check on a lite VM and proposes a fix with the check's output.

Its walls: no cloud credentials in the VM, and never tofu or terraform apply or destroy, argocd app sync or workflow_dispatch. G3's guard rails also block these commands. A person applies anything that touches cloud resources.

Editing .github/workflows/ needs GitHub's workflows permission, which the rhino-ai-agents App does not have. Until Security agrees to a grant for this fixer only, it posts workflow changes as a patch on the ticket. A person applies it.
sections.because: Workflow files can be weakened in ways test regexes never see, like switching a job off. So they get their own rules.

notes.text: Workflow files are parsed as YAML to compare jobs.
A failing step that no longer fails the job.
if: false, plain or as ${{ false }}.
A command ending in || true or || exit 0 can never fail.
Flags that turn a check off, such as --no-verify or -check=false.
Input: the diff and the required check names from G0's ruleset.
Only workflow files are checked here.
Every added line against every weakener.
The check names before and after the change.
A required check that disappears is a false heal.

sections.h: The pipeline fixer, part 2: narrowed triggers
p: A subtle weakener: narrowing a workflow's trigger paths, so the check stops running on some changes. If the new path list is a strict subset of the old one, it is a finding.

Done means the failing check passes in the VM. Add a plan or rendered diff from CI when one exists. Today infrastructure CI only checks formatting, so the PR says plainly that no plan was run. Triggers come from the copies of the trigger Action in infrastructure and gitops.
sections.because: A check that no longer runs is as weak as a check that always passes.

notes.text: The paths: filters of the workflow's triggers, before and after.
Fewer paths, and every new path was already there: the trigger was narrowed.
The finding says what that means: the check stops running on some changes.
These findings join the general ones. Any finding rejects the run.
Parse the YAML and list jobs.
A job's check name is its name: if set, else its id.

callout.text: The G5-25 sketch calls triggerPaths, but no ticket defines it. Write it next to jobNames: parse the workflow YAML and collect the on.<event>.paths lists into a Set. Add a test for it, since the check depends on it.

quiz.q: The fe-ci-fixer runs the failed commands at main's head in the VM, and they pass. What does it do?

options.text: Pushes a no-op commit to re-trigger CI
options.why: Nova and the routines never re-run or dispatch CI; there is also nothing to fix.

options.text: Posts the evidence to #ai-agents-alerts and stops: environment or flake
options.why: Green in the VM means the code is not the problem.

options.text: Fixes the most likely file anyway
options.why: That is exactly the fix of code that is not broken that check_main_first prevents.

quiz.q: A fix changes fail_under = 50 to fail_under = 40. What does the false-heal check report for a routine?

options.text: Nothing; it is a config file, not a test
options.why: Thresholds are checked in every file, not only tests.

options.text: fail_under loosened 50 -> 40, and the run is rejected as false_heal
options.why: For fail-under, lower is looser. For routines any finding rejects the run.

options.text: A flag in the PR, and a person decides
options.why: That is the behaviour for Nova. For routines it is a rejection.

quiz.q: The pipeline fixer's fix changes .github/workflows/infra-lint.yml. How does it reach the repo today?

options.text: It pushes the change through the broker
options.why: The rhino-ai-agents App has no workflows permission, so a push to workflow files is refused.

options.text: It posts the change as a patch on the ticket for a person to apply
options.why: Until Security agrees to a pipeline-fixer-only grant.

options.text: It runs gh workflow run to test it first
options.why: workflow_dispatch is never allowed for agents.

words.plain: A fix that turns CI green by weakening a test or a check instead of fixing the cause.
The CI fixer's first step: run the failed commands at main's head in the VM.
A data file per CI fixer that maps each CI job to the commands that reproduce it, and names hand-offs.
A failure the routine must not fix; it posts the evidence and gives it to a person or team.
Generated gRPC stubs out of step with the .proto files: the cloud-client contract.
A number a check compares against, such as fail-under, retries or a timeout.
